questions.prompt: How many bones are in an adult human body?
questions.explain: Babies have about 300; many fuse as they grow.

questions.prompt: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explain: The liver is the largest internal organ.

questions.prompt: What is the longest bone in the body?
questions.explain: The femur, or thigh bone, is about a quarter of your height.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest bone in the body?
questions.explain: The stirrup bone in the middle ear is about 3 mm long.

questions.prompt: What does the heart pump around the body?
questions.explain: Blood carries oxygen and food to every cell.

questions.prompt: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explain: Two atria and two ventricles.

questions.prompt: Which organ do you breathe with?
questions.explain: They swap oxygen and carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: Which gas do we breathe out more of than we breathe in?
questions.explain: Our cells make carbon dioxide as waste.

questions.prompt: Which organ makes insulin?
questions.explain: Insulin controls the level of sugar in the blood.

questions.prompt: What is the hardest substance in the human body?
questions.explain: Enamel is mostly a hard mineral.

questions.prompt: How many teeth does an adult usually have?
questions.explain: Including four wisdom teeth.

questions.prompt: How many baby teeth do children have?
questions.explain: They are replaced by 32 adult teeth.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells carry oxygen?
questions.explain: Haemoglobin in them carries oxygen.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells fight germs?
questions.explain: They are part of the immune system.

questions.prompt: Which tiny pieces in the blood help it clot when you cut yourself?
questions.explain: They clump together to plug the wound.

questions.prompt: Which is the biggest muscle in the body?
questions.explain: It is the main muscle of the buttocks.

questions.prompt: What is the coloured part of the eye called?
questions.explain: The pupil is the black hole in the middle of it.

questions.prompt: Which organ filters blood to make urine?
questions.explain: Urine is then stored in the bladder.

questions.prompt: What does the skull protect?
questions.explain: The rib cage protects the heart and lungs.

questions.prompt: What is the normal human body temperature, roughly?
questions.explain: It varies a little through the day.

questions.prompt: How many senses are traditionally counted?
questions.explain: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch; scientists count others too, like balance.

questions.prompt: Which part of the body do you smell with?
questions.explain: Smell also helps you taste food.

questions.prompt: You can live with only one kidney.
questions.explain: One healthy kidney can do the work of two.

questions.prompt: Babies are born with more bones than adults.
questions.explain: About 300 bones fuse into 206.

questions.prompt: Your heart is on the far left of your chest.
questions.explain: It sits near the middle, tilted slightly to the left.

questions.prompt: Where in the body are red blood cells made?
questions.explain: Marrow inside big bones makes millions every second.

questions.prompt: What are the tiny air sacs in the lungs called?
questions.explain: Oxygen passes into the blood through their thin walls.

questions.prompt: Which organ is the body's main chemical factory and can regrow?
questions.explain: It can regrow from as little as a quarter of its tissue.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the tube that carries food from your mouth to your stomach?
questions.explain: The trachea, or windpipe, carries air.

questions.prompt: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explain: Veins carry blood back to the heart.

questions.prompt: What joins muscles to bones?
questions.explain: Ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.prompt: Put the path of food in order.
questions.explain: Most nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine.
